na-chornobyl-1986.n: Chornobyl (Chernobyl) Nuclear Power Plant Unit 4 accident
na-chornobyl-1986.loc: Chornobyl NPP, Pripyat, Kyiv Oblast, Kiev, UKR
na-chornobyl-1986.cp: SSE Chornobyl NPP contacts page: published point for the ChNPP industrial site in the exclusion zone
na-chornobyl-1986.st: Exclusion zone in force; NSC damaged by the Feb 2025 drone strike and fire, repairs coordinated by EBRD.
na-chornobyl-1986.what: Power surge during a reactor systems test destroyed Unit 4 on 26 Apr 1986; the explosion and following fire released massive amounts of radioactive material (NRC). 28 of the site's ~600 workers died of severe radiation effects in the first four months and 106 more had acute radiation sickness; ~115,000 people were evacuated in 1986 and ~220,000 later; 30 km exclusion zone (NRC, citing UNSCEAR 2008). Turbogenerator trip signal blocked at 01:23:04 (INSAG-7). Rated INES 7 (BABS). New Safe Confinement completed and handed over in 2019; struck by a drone on 14 Feb 2025 (EBRD), after which the IAEA found the NSC cannot currently perform its two main safety functions (GOV/2026/7).
fig: 28 workers died of acute radiation effects within four months; 2 died on site of non-radiological causes; 106 ARS cases (NRC)
Exclusion zone in force; NSC damaged by the Feb 2025 drone strike and fire, repairs coordinated by EBRD.

na-kyshtym-1957.n: Kyshtym accident: waste-tank explosion at the Mayak Production Association
na-kyshtym-1957.loc: Mayak PA near Ozyorsk (Kyshtym), Chelyabinsk Oblast, Chelyabinsk, RUS
na-kyshtym-1957.st: EURT partly a state nature reserve; Mayak operating (not re-verified).
na-kyshtym-1957.what: Cooling failure in a concrete tank of highly active nitrate-acetate waste led to a chemical explosion that released fission products over Chelyabinsk, Sverdlovsk and Tyumen provinces; about 2 million Ci dispersed off the site; the 0.1 Ci/km2 Sr-90 trace reached 300 km (INFCIRC/368). About 600 people were evacuated within 7-10 days and about 10,000 later (INFCIRC/368). Tank 14 destroyed, no deaths; ~20 MCi total, 90% fell on the production site; contaminated area named the East Urals Radioactive Trace (EURT); later ranked INES 6 (Mayak PA, 2013).
fig: chemical explosion of a high-level liquid-waste storage tank
